questions.title: Two-node KCL
questions.prompt: Node a connects to ground through 4 Ω and to node b through 2 Ω. Node b connects to ground through 6 Ω. A 3 A source enters a from ground; a 1 A source leaves b for ground. Write KCL at both nodes and find Va.
questions.solution: Solving gives Va=6 V and Vb=3 V. Substitute: 6/4+(6−3)/2=3 A; 3/6+(3−6)/2=−1 A.
hints: Apply KCL separately at a and b.
Check both source directions before solving.
questions.origin: Original StudyLab practice question; the reference covers the concept, not this question.

questions.title: Supernode with reversed polarity
questions.prompt: Node a connects to ground through 4 Ω, node b through 2 Ω, and a 3 A source enters b from ground. A 4 V source has + at b and − at a. Write supernode KCL and the source constraint. Find Va.
questions.solution: Vb=Va+4. Then Va/4+(Va+4)/2=3, giving Va=4/3 V and Vb=16/3 V.
hints: Enclose the voltage source and both nodes.
KCL around the supernode has the external resistor and current-source branches.
The positive terminal is at b: Vb−Va=4 V.
questions.origin: Original StudyLab practice question; the reference covers the concept, not this question.

questions.title: Shared-resistor mesh
questions.prompt: A clockwise left mesh contains a 12 V rise and a shared 6 Ω resistor. A clockwise right mesh contains that shared 6 Ω resistor and separate 2 Ω and 4 Ω resistors. Use KVL to find the clockwise left mesh current i1.
questions.solution: The first loop gives i1−i2=2 A. The second gives i2=i1/2. Thus i1=4 A and i2=2 A.
hints: Shared-resistor current is i1−i2 in the left mesh.
questions.origin: Original StudyLab practice question; the reference covers the concept, not this question.

questions.title: Supermesh constraint
questions.prompt: A 12 V source drives the outer perimeter of two clockwise meshes. The outer-left resistance is 2 Ω, the outer-right resistance is 6 Ω, and a 1 A source in their shared branch points with i1 and against i2. Write outer KVL and the source constraint; find i2.
questions.solution: Substitute i1=i2+1 into 2i1+6i2=12: 8i2=10, so i2=1.25 A and i1=2.25 A.
hints: Bypass the current-source branch in KVL.
Use the source arrow to form the mesh-current difference.
questions.origin: Original StudyLab practice question; the reference covers the concept, not this question.

questions.title: Book 4.6 · Single-node voltage
questions.prompt: Use nodal analysis. A 24 V source (+ at top) reaches node x through series 20 Ω and 80 Ω resistors. From x to ground are a 25 Ω resistor and a 40 mA current source pointing downward. Write KCL at x and find Vx across the 25 Ω resistor (+ at x).
questions.solution: The two series resistors carry (Vx−24)/100 A from x. KCL gives (Vx−24)/100+Vx/25+0.04=0, so 5Vx=20 and Vx=4 V. The 25 Ω branch current is 0.16 A downward.
hints: Combine the 20 Ω and 80 Ω series resistors.
questions.origin: Adapted from Nilsson/Riedel Problem 4.6; circuit values and connections follow the cited problem.

questions.title: Book 4.13 · Two-node KCL
questions.prompt: Use the bottom wire as ground. A 6 A source injects into node a; 40 Ω joins a to ground. An 8 Ω resistor joins a to b. At b, 80 Ω and 120 Ω each connect to ground, while a 1 A source points from b to ground. Write both KCL equations and find Vb.
questions.solution: The two KCL equations give Va=120 V and Vb=96 V. Check at a: 120/40+(120−96)/8=6 A. At b: 96/80+96/120+(96−120)/8=−1 A.
hints: Label the two top nodes a and b.
Apply KCL with injected source current positive.
questions.origin: Adapted from Nilsson/Riedel Problem 4.13; circuit values and connections follow the cited problem.

questions.title: Book 4.22 · Voltage-source supernode
questions.prompt: Use the bottom wire as ground. Node b connects to ground through 50 Ω and a 2 A current source pointing downward. A 25 V source connects b (+) to node c (−). Node c connects to ground through 150 Ω and through series 20 Ω + 55 Ω. Write supernode KCL and the source constraint. Find Vb, measured from b to ground.
questions.solution: The outside branches of the supernode give (Vb+Vc)/50=−2 A, so Vb+Vc=−100 V. With Vb−Vc=25 V, Vb=−37.5 V and Vc=−62.5 V. The negative sign follows the declared voltage direction.
hints: Include b and c in one supernode.
questions.origin: Adapted from Nilsson/Riedel Problem 4.22; circuit values and connections follow the cited problem.

questions.title: Book 4.32 · Reversed branch current
questions.prompt: Use clockwise mesh currents i1 (left) and i2 (right). The left loop has an 80 V source (+ at top), a 75 Ω top resistor and a 125 Ω bottom resistor. The right loop has a 140 V source (+ at top), a 150 Ω top resistor and a 250 Ω bottom resistor. The loops share a 200 Ω vertical resistor. The requested current ic through the 150 Ω resistor points right-to-left, opposite clockwise i2. Write mesh KVL and find ic.
questions.solution: Mesh KVL gives i1=0.38 A and i2=0.36 A. The requested arrow through 150 Ω points opposite i2, so ic=−0.36 A. The negative value says current actually flows left-to-right.
hints: The shared 200 Ω drop is 200(i1−i2) in the left loop.
questions.origin: Adapted from Nilsson/Riedel Problem 4.32(a); circuit values and connections follow the cited problem.

questions.title: Book 4.49 · Supermesh power
questions.prompt: Two clockwise meshes share a 4 A current source pointing downward. The left outer branch has a 100 V source (+ at top), a 6 Ω top resistor and a 9 Ω bottom resistor. The right outer branch has a 25 V source (+ at bottom), a 20 Ω top resistor and a 30 Ω bottom resistor. Use a supermesh and calculate the total power dissipated by the four resistors.
questions.solution: The shared-source constraint is i1−i2=4 A. Outer KVL is 15i1+50i2=100+25=125 V. Thus i1=5 A and i2=1 A; resistor power is (6+9)5²+(20+30)1²=425 W.
hints: The 4 A source is inside the supermesh.
Write KVL around the outer perimeter and a separate source-current constraint.
questions.origin: Adapted from Nilsson/Riedel Problem 4.49; circuit values and connections follow the cited problem.

questions.title: Superposition at a node
questions.prompt: A 6 V source connects to node x through 3 Ω; node x connects to ground through 6 Ω. An independent 1 A source injects current from ground into x. Use superposition to find Vx. Show each source contribution.
questions.solution: With the 1 A source opened, voltage division gives 6·6/(3+6)=4 V. With the 6 V source shorted, 1 A sees 3||6=2 Ω, giving 2 V. Total Vx=6 V. Direct KCL: (Vx−6)/3+Vx/6=1.
hints: Keep one independent source active at a time.
Short the ideal voltage source; open the ideal current source.
Add the two voltage contributions algebraically.
questions.origin: Original StudyLab practice question; the reference covers the concept, not this question.

questions.title: Source transformation
questions.prompt: An ideal 2 A source points upward in parallel with a 5 Ω resistor. Transform it to its Thévenin equivalent. Find the open-circuit voltage at the top terminal relative to the bottom terminal.
questions.solution: Open-circuit current through the parallel resistor is 2 A downward, so Vth=(2 A)(5 Ω)=10 V with the top terminal positive. The equivalent series resistor remains 5 Ω.
hints: Use the current source and its parallel resistor as a pair.
Check the voltage polarity from the source arrow.
questions.origin: Original StudyLab practice question; the reference covers the concept, not this question.

questions.title: Thévenin open-circuit voltage
questions.prompt: A 12 V source feeds a 3 kΩ resistor to terminal a. A 6 kΩ resistor connects a to terminal b (ground). With the load removed, find Vth=Vab.
questions.solution: The open-circuit terminal voltage is the divider output: 12×6/(3+6)=8 V. With the source set to zero, Rth=3 kΩ||6 kΩ=2 kΩ.
hints: The 3 kΩ and 6 kΩ resistors form a divider.
questions.origin: Original StudyLab practice question; the reference covers the concept, not this question.

questions.title: Norton equivalent
questions.prompt: A 9 V ideal source in series with 3 Ω appears at terminals a–b, with a positive relative to b. Find the Norton source current from b to a.
questions.solution: A 9 V source in series with 3 Ω has short-circuit current 9/3=3 A. The Norton current arrow points b→a, with a 3 Ω parallel resistance.
hints: Check the Norton arrow needed to make a positive at open circuit.
questions.origin: Original StudyLab practice question; the reference covers the concept, not this question.

questions.title: Maximum power transfer
questions.prompt: A network has Vth=8 V and Rth=2 kΩ. Choose the load for maximum power, then calculate that maximum power in mW.
questions.solution: For a resistive DC load, RL=2 kΩ. Pmax=8²/(4×2000)=0.008 W=8 mW.
hints: Match the load to the Thévenin resistance.
At the match, the load gets half the Thévenin voltage.
questions.origin: Original StudyLab practice question; the reference covers the concept, not this question.

questions.title: Series capacitors and energy
questions.prompt: A 6 μF capacitor and a 3 μF capacitor are in series across a 12 V ideal source. Find the total stored energy in μJ after steady state.
questions.solution: Ceq=2 μF. Total stored energy is 0.5×2 μF×(12 V)²=144 μJ. The same charge appears on both series capacitors.
hints: Find Ceq before computing total energy.
questions.origin: Original StudyLab practice question; the reference covers the concept, not this question.

questions.title: Inductor voltage
questions.prompt: A 50 mH inductor current increases at 4 A/s under passive sign convention. Find the voltage across it in V.
questions.solution: L=0.05 H; vL=(0.05 H)(4 A/s)=0.2 V, positive at the current-entry terminal.
hints: The rising current makes vL positive in passive convention.
questions.origin: Original StudyLab practice question; the reference covers the concept, not this question.

questions.title: Parallel inductors and energy
questions.prompt: Two uncoupled inductors of 12 mH and 6 mH are in parallel. Both start with zero current. After a source establishes a total current of 3 A, find their total stored energy in mJ.
questions.solution: With zero initial currents, the branch currents divide to 1 A in 12 mH and 2 A in 6 mH. Their energies sum to ½(12 mH)(1 A)²+½(6 mH)(2 A)²=18 mJ. Equivalently Leq=4 mH and W=½Leq(3 A)².
hints: Use the parallel equivalent for uncoupled inductors.
questions.origin: Original StudyLab practice question; the reference covers the concept, not this question.

questions.title: Natural RC response
questions.prompt: A 100 μF capacitor initially holds 12 V. At t=0 it discharges through 10 kΩ. Find its voltage at t=1 s in V.
questions.solution: The time constant is (10,000 Ω)(100 μF)=1 s. v(1)=12e⁻¹≈4.415 V.
questions.origin: Original StudyLab practice question; the reference covers the concept, not this question.

questions.title: Natural RL response
questions.prompt: An inductor L=200 mH initially carries 2 A and then discharges through R=10 Ω. Find i at t=40 ms in A.
questions.solution: τ=0.2/10=0.02 s. At 0.04 s, i=2e⁻²≈0.271 A. Inductor current is continuous at switching.
hints: The initial inductor current continues through t=0.
questions.origin: Original StudyLab practice question; the reference covers the concept, not this question.

questions.title: Series RLC damping
questions.prompt: A source-free series RLC circuit has R=4 Ω, L=1 H, and C=0.25 F. Compute α/ω0. Then state in your working whether the circuit is overdamped, critically damped, or underdamped.
questions.solution: α/ω0=1, so the circuit is critically damped. Its repeated pole is s=−2 s⁻¹.
hints: Use the series RLC form of α.
Find ω0 from L and C.
questions.origin: Original StudyLab practice question; the reference covers the concept, not this question.

questions.title: Parallel RLC damped frequency
questions.prompt: A source-free parallel RLC circuit has R=2 Ω, C=0.25 F, and L=1 H. Find its damped angular frequency ωd in rad/s. State the damping case in your working.
questions.solution: Since α=1<2=ω0, the circuit is underdamped and ωd=√3≈1.732 rad/s.
hints: Use the parallel RLC form of α.
questions.origin: Original StudyLab practice question; the reference covers the concept, not this question.

questions.title: Critically damped natural current
questions.prompt: A source-free series RLC circuit has R=2 Ω, L=1 H, C=1 F, i(0+)=0 A, and di/dt at 0+ equal to 4 A/s. Find i(1 s) in A.
questions.solution: α=R/(2L)=1 and ω0=1, so the response is critical. i(0)=0 gives A1=0; i′(0)=4 gives A2=4 A/s. Thus i(t)=4te⁻ᵗ A and i(1)=4/e≈1.472 A.
hints: Apply i(0) and i′(0) to find A1 and A2.
questions.origin: Original StudyLab practice question; the reference covers the concept, not this question.

questions.title: Series RLC step response
questions.prompt: A series RLC circuit has R=2 Ω, L=1 H, C=1 F. Its capacitor starts at 0 V and its inductor current at 0 A. A 10 V DC step is applied at t=0. Find vC(1 s) in V.
questions.solution: The circuit is critically damped (α=ω0=1 s⁻¹). The initial value and slope are zero, and the final value is 10 V. Therefore vC(1)=10(1−2/e)≈2.642 V.
hints: Find α, ω0, and the DC final capacitor voltage.
questions.origin: Original StudyLab practice question; the reference covers the concept, not this question.
